card.name: Inside words in all-caps warnings
card.fires_on: The last piece of a word, or occasionally a nearby small word or number, in ALL-CAPS warning text from drug labels. Examples are ELECTROLY-TE, EAR-LY, SER-UM and CARE-FUL.

modes.label: Word endings in caps
modes.description: Final piece of a long capitalized word that is split into parts, such as TE, LY, UM, FUL or ATE.
modes.example: ROCHLORIDE AND ATROPINE SULFATE SHOULD BE ACCOMPANIED BY APPROPRIATE FLUID AND ELECTROLY<<TE>> THERAPY, WHEN INDIC

modes.label: Small word or number in caps
modes.description: A short word or number in capitalized text, less common than word endings.
modes.example: VERE HEPATIC DYSFUNCTION FOLLOWED SUBSEQUENTLY BY LIVER FAILURE WAS <<3>> WEEKS AFTER INITIATION OF F

card.writes: It promotes capitalized letter groups like CH, TH and PH, which suggests it helps the model continue in all-caps text.
card.plain: It fires on the end of a word in a capitalized label warning, where the next word is also expected in capitals.
